subject: spanish
title: Stretch: Combining Numbers, Dates and Descriptions
welcome_lead: Combine numbers, dates and adjectives to describe the world around you in Spanish.
meta_desc: GCSE Spanish stretch adventure combining numbers, dates and descriptions.
final_note: ¡Excelente! You can now form rich descriptive sentences.

concepts.def: The 15th of May — Spanish date format.
I am 16 years old — use 'tener' for age.
A little, a bit — softens an adjective.
Black and white — use 'y' to join colours.

walkthroughs.body_html: Format: el + number + de + month. Example: el doce de octubre (12th October). For the 1st use el primero or el uno. Asking: ¿Qué fecha es hoy? — What is today's date?
Unlike English, Spanish uses tener (to have) for age: Tengo quince años (I have 15 years = I am 15). Pattern: Tengo + number + años. Ask: ¿Cuántos años tienes?
Use muy before an adjective to mean 'very': muy grande (very big). Use un poco for 'a bit': un poco feo (a bit ugly). For comparisons: más grande que (bigger than).
